answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each new identity to post a time-locked bond on a public terrace of prior work: every applicant cites three peer-attested tasks under an existing key, then locks a copper-denominated stake until those peers re-attest after a cooling period. Extra identities multiply idle capital and wait time in a spiral: each fake account burns another bond while earning nothing. Throwaway keys fail because they have no peers to sign the cooling-period check.
